(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI) This appeal is filed by the appellant/petitioner being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Court of X Addl. District and Sessions Judge and Addl. MACT, Belagavi ('Tribunal' for short) vide judgment and award dated 10.02.2020 passed in MVC No.600 of 2019.

entities.text: X Addl. District and Sessions Judge
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
2.1.
On 28.01.2019, the petitioner was proceeding on a Bajaj motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-22/EN-5829 as a pillion rider from Khanapur towards Toppinkatti.
On Jatt- Jamboti road near Lokoli cross, a truck bearing Reg.No.KA- 22/B-3732 came from a rear side, and dashed to the motorcycle.
As a result, the rider of the motorcycle lost control over the vehicle and the rider died on the spot.
The petitioner sustained a grievous injuries to his both legs.
He was admitted as the inpatient from 28.01.2019 to 11.02.2019 and incurred huge medical expenses.

The NC: 2026:KHC-D:3637 HC-KAR petitioner filed a claim petition in MVC No.600 of 2019 before the Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking a compensation on account of the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
The legal representatives of the deceased rider of the motorcycle have also filed a claim petition in MVC No. 601 of 2019.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petitions.
The Tribunal clubbed both the claim petitions.
2.2. The owner of the offending truck filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition.
It was also denied that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the truck.
It is contented that, the truck is insured with respondent No.2/Insurance Company and the driver of the truck possessed a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of the accident.
Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petition against the owner of the truck.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that, the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of accident; the rider Narayan Huvani Halgekar vs Rama Mashnu Kadam on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84707438/
2 and the pillion rider were not wearing helmets; the motorcycle was not insured with the Insurance Company, and the owner of the motorcycle is a necessary party.

entities.text: Narayan Huvani Halgekar vs Rama Mashnu Kadam
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the petition suffers from non-joinder of necessary party.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the claim petition against the Insurance Company.
2.4. Based on the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal framed the separate issues and recorded the common evidence.

2.5. To substantiate their case, the petitioner in MVC No.600 of 2019 examined himself as PW1,
examined the Doctor as PW2; petitioner No.1 in MVC No. 601 of 2019 was examined as PW3 and 27 documents were marked as NC: 2026:KHC-D:3637 HC-KAR Exs.P1 to P27.
The respondents have not led any oral evidence, but marked 1 document as Ex.R1 with consent.

2.6. The Tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition (MVC No.600 of 2019) in part with costs vide judgment dated 10.02.2020, and awarded a compensation of 19,16,752/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of the petition till its realisation, and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest.
3. The petitioner in MVC No.600 of 2019, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, filed this appeal.

4. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner aged about 32 years as of the date of NC: 2026:KHC-D:3637 HC-KAR accident and due to accident, he has suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 80%, wherein the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 70%, which is on the lower side.

He further submits that, the petitioner has not produced any income proof; in the absence of income proof, the Tribunal could have taken the notional income as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The Tribunal has taken the notional income at 11,000/-, which is on the lower side.
He further submits that, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads is also on the lower side.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that, the Tribunal was justified in fixing the notional income at 11,000/- in the absence of income proof.

He further submits that, the petitioner examined the Doctor as PW2, wherein the Tribunal, after assessing the evidence of PW2,
has rightly assessed the permanent disability at 70% to the whole body, which is just and NC:
2026:KHC-D:3637 HC-KAR proper.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads is also reasonable.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to dismiss the appeal.

7. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: 8. The point that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.
9. It is undisputed that the petitioner and his friend deceased Somanath Parashram Halagekar were proceeding on a motorcycle on 28.01.2019 wherein, the petitioner was a pillion rider.
A truck bearing Reg.No.KA-22/EN-5829 came from the rear side and dashed to the motorcycle.

As a result,
the rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries and the rider succumbed to the injuries.
The petitioner has produced the charge sheet marked as Ex.P7, which discloses that it is filed against the driver of the truck.

The Tribunal was justified in recording the finding NC:
2026:KHC-D:3637 HC-KAR that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the truck.
Reg. Quantum of compensation:
10. The petitioner was aged about 32 years as of the date of accident and contends that, he was a Mason and was earning 15,000/- per month.
To substantiate his case, he has not produced any income proof.
In the absence of income proof, the notional income has to be assessed as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As the accident is of 2019, the notional income is assessed at 13,250/- per month.

In view of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1, 40% future prospects has to be added to the monthly income i.e., 13,250/- + 40%
(5,300/-) = 18,550/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The multiplier applicable to the age group of the petitioner is '16'.

The petitioner, to prove the disability, has (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2026:KHC-D:3637 HC-KAR examined the Doctor as PW2, who is not a treated Doctor, has issued the disability certificate marked as Ex.P16 and has deposed that, he has assessed the disability to the crush injury left leg from knee joint and below with vascular injury and has opined that the petitioner has sustained permanent physical disability to the lower limb to the extent of 80%, the petitioner was operated and his left knee was amputated due to crush injury and the petitioner's left leg can be fitted with artificial limb.
He has opined that the petitioner has suffered a physical disability of 80% to the lower limb, and the Tribunal has taken the disability at 70% to the whole body, which is just and proper.
